family: War and emergency orders (First World War measures, Alien Property Custodian sales, eight-hour suspensions, one air-space reservation)

mechanisms.description: P1: an order whose only operative content revokes or rescinds another order, dissolves a body another order created, or restores powers is spent on issue. P2: an order whose only operative content amends another order (its operative words say 'is hereby amended', 'hereby amend', 'is hereby revoked; and in place thereof') merges into the parent on issue; its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends. EO 3176, which itself takes title to all seized enemy vessels, is a single self-executing act done on issue.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The order's date (an order that states a later effective hour is spent at that hour).

mechanisms.description: An order that states its own end: a fixed day (EO 3233, EO 6023), the duration of the war (EO 2652), or the war plus six months after a treaty of peace is proclaimed (EO 2929).
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The stated day, read inclusively; for war-keyed terms, no later than the proclamation of the last 1921 peace treaty (Dec. 20, 1921) or six months after it (June 20, 1922).

mechanisms.description: COORDINATOR_RULINGS P7: EO 3320 terminated and abolished by name the United States Food Administration 'and all remaining divisions and branches thereof' and 'the executive administration and office created by said Executive Order of May 14, 1919' (the Wheat Director), and confined the Grain Corporation to liquidation, 'continuing to act as a governmental agency for this purpose only'. An order whose only continuing command is the creation of one of those offices, or a command exercised only through them, ends with them.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Aug. 21, 1920 (fixed for orders the abolition names; for the others, no later than that day).

mechanisms.description: EO 3154 provided that the Committee on Public Information would cease 'upon such relinquishment and transfer' of its papers and property to the Council of National Defense. The held text makes the end conditional on a transfer no held record shows; the National Archives dates the abolition to Aug. 21, 1919, but that finding aid is not held.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Date of the transfer (not held); NARA gives Aug. 21, 1919.

mechanisms.description: COORDINATOR_RULINGS P8. The Lever Act sec. 24 provides that 'the provisions of this Act shall cease to be in effect when the existing state of war between the United States and Germany shall have terminated', and that the fact and date of that termination 'shall be ascertained and proclaimed by the President'. 41 Stat. 1359-1360 displaces that mode of fixing the date ('notwithstanding any provision in any Act of Congress or joint resolution providing any other mode of determining the date of such termination'), treats March 3, 1921 as the date, and does not except the Lever Act. An order whose only operative content is a delegation of the Act's powers (or a direction how the delegate is to exercise them), and which rests on the Lever Act alone, ends with them: the ceasing words reach the very provisions delegated, so the delegate has nothing left to exercise. An order that also invokes other authority ('and other powers vested in me by law') is not reached as a whole and stays open. This differs from a repeal of the authority to make new orders (FLPMA sec. 704(a)), where existing orders keep operative effect of their own.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: No later than March 3, 1921 (interval from the order's date).

mechanisms.description: COORDINATOR_RULINGS P8. The Overman Act provides: 'Upon the termination of this Act all executive or administrative agencies ... shall exercise the same functions, duties, and powers as heretofore or as hereafter by law may be provided, any authorization of the President under this Act to the contrary notwithstanding.' Those words reach only authorizations under that Act. An order whose only operative content is a reassignment of functions authorized by the Act, and which rests on the Act alone, ends with it. An order that also invokes 'any and all other Acts of Congress' or 'all other powers thereto me enabling', or that rests on another statute (EO 2868 on the Council of National Defense provisions of 1916), is not reached as a whole and stays open, with the Act's end disclosed as a candidate.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Between Sept. 3, 1921 (six months after March 3, 1921 under S1) and June 20, 1922 (six months after the last treaty proclamation); claimed as an interval from the order's date to June 20, 1922.

mechanisms.description: COORDINATOR_RULINGS P8. The emergency shipping fund section of the Act of June 15, 1917 provides: 'All authority granted to the President herein, or by him delegated, shall cease six months after a final treaty of peace is proclaimed between this Government and the German Empire.' The Act of Apr. 22, 1918 (ch. 62) amended that section 'by adding a new provision' (clause (f), street and interurban railways) and by adding words to paragraph (b), so its powers are part of the section the cessation sentence calls 'herein'. The Act of Oct. 6, 1917 raised the section's cost limits. The 'Emergency shipping fund' sections of the Acts of July 1, 1918 and Nov. 4, 1918 have not been read, so powers granted by them are not shown to fall within 'herein'. An order whose only operative content is a delegation of powers granted by the 1917 section as amended ends with them; an order that delegates powers under the unread 1918 sections stays open.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: No later than May 14, 1922 (six months after Nov. 14, 1921); Sept. 3, 1921 if S1 is read to govern that clause.

mechanisms.description: EO 3019-A ordered the War Industries Board and its subordinate bodies to 'terminate and dissolve on' January 1, 1919, with exceptions: officials continued 'for such limited period after January 1, 1919 as may be necessary ... but in no event longer than the proclamation of peace'; the Price Fixing Committee continued until prices already fixed expired; the Planning and Statistics and Wool Division functions were transferred to other bodies until completed; and the Board continued 'for the sole and only purpose of winding up'. The order rests on the Overman Act 'as well as ... any and all other Acts of Congress', so the Overman Act's end does not by itself reach it; its own 'proclamation of peace' cap covers only the first exception and turns on a treaty proclamation date that is not held.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Not fixed: Jan. 1, 1919 for the Board's main body; the continuations end on unheld dates (proclamation of peace, expiry of fixed prices, completion of transferred functions).
The revoking order's date (Sept. 6, 1918 for EO 2952); EO 3180 operates as of July 14, 1919 though issued Nov. 25, 1919.

mechanisms.description: The National Archives records the War Trade Board as abolished effective June 30, 1919 under EOs 3059 and 3086-A; the held orders only authorize the transfer 'whenever ... expedient', so that date is a disclosed earlier candidate, not a held basis.

S1 fixes March 3, 1921 as the end of the war for Acts, joint resolutions and proclamations contingent on it. It ends no order by itself: it reaches an order only through the statute the order rests on, does not govern an executive order's own words such as 'during the war', and excepts the Trading with the Enemy Act.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: March 3, 1921, only through a statute that by its terms depends on the war's end.

mechanisms.description: Alien Property Custodian functions were transferred: EO 6694 (May 1, 1934) to the Department of Justice; EO 9095 (Mar. 11, 1942) created a new Office of Alien Property Custodian, and EO 9142 (Apr. 21, 1942) gave it the functions, personnel and property of the Justice Department's Alien Property Division; EO 9788 (Oct. 14, 1946) terminated that office and vested its functions and property in the Attorney General; EO 11281 (May 13, 1966) recites the Office of Alien Property's abolition by June 30, 1966 and moves the EO 8389 blocking controls to Treasury. A transfer of functions carries an authorization forward; none of these instruments, nor the Knox-Porter Resolution's sec. 5, extinguishes a First World War sale authorization.

An order authorizing the Custodian (or Frank L. Polk as delegate) to sell, reject bids for, resell or release named property is exhausted when that act is done; the order sets no deadline, so whether and when it was done must come from a record of the act. The Custodian's reports are the general record; a held later order that records the act decides its parent (M16).
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: The date of sale, rejection or release, from the Custodian's reports (not held).

mechanisms.description: An eight-hour suspension or waiver for named work or contracts ends when that work is completed, on a stated term, or by a further order. Two authorities are used. Sec. 2 of the Act of June 19, 1912 lets the President waive the Act 'as to any specific contract' 'during time of war or a time when war is imminent': a war-contingent power. The proviso of the Act of Mar. 4, 1917 (39 Stat. 1192) lets the President suspend the eight-hour law 'in case of national emergency'. Whether 41 Stat. 1359 reaches either power is unsettled: its words govern the construction of Acts 'containing provisions contingent upon the duration' of the 1917 war and of the 'present or existing emergency, meaning thereby the war', and say nothing about waivers already granted for specific contracts. A waiver granted is an exercise of the power, not a delegation of it, so P8 does not apply; the resolution's date (March 3, 1921) is a disclosed candidate end only.
An order whose operative content is one act for one named person (an appointment or a designation to act) follows PD-CS-ONE-PERSON (COORDINATOR_RULINGS P4).

A single sale authorization is exhausted by performance when a held later instrument records that the authorized sale was made. EO 3265 (Apr. 29, 1920) corrects EO 3259's schedule so that it corresponds 'with the terms of the actual sale made by the Alien Property Custodian'.
mechanisms.effective_date_rule: Interval from the authorizing order's date to the date of the instrument recording the sale (EO 3259: Apr. 16 to Apr. 29, 1920).

Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing

when.text_regex: (?:is|are|be) hereby (?:amended|modified|changed)|hereby amend|amended (?:so as )?to read|is amended|hereby revoked; and in place thereof

Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.

Disclosure: its text continues as part of the parent until the parent ends; the parent's lifecycle carries it.

EO 3265's parent EO 3259 is itself decided (B03E, exhausted by performance by Apr. 29, 1920).

procedure.description: EO 3176: the order itself takes possession and title of all seized enemy vessels.

lead.basis: The order's only operative words are 'the possession and title of the United States in all such vessels is taken over in accordance with Joint Resolution ... May 12, 1917': a single act done by the order itself on issue. The title is a surviving consequence.

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing

procedure.description: EO 3259 (sale of 4,505 First Reinsurance Co. shares to the Security Trust Company as syndicate manager): a held later order records the actual sale.

when.text_regex: authorized to sell at private sale

lead.basis: EO 3259 (Apr. 16, 1920) authorizes one private sale of named property and nothing else. EO 3265 (Apr. 29, 1920, held) corrects its schedule so that it corresponds 'with the offer made by The Security Trust Company as Syndicate Manager, and with the terms of the actual sale made by the Alien Property Custodian'. The single authorized act was therefore done after the order's date and by Apr. 29, 1920, and the authorization was exhausted by performance. EO 3265's words that EO 3259 'shall be deemed to be in full force and effect' confirm the authorization as corrected; they command nothing further. The shares sold are a surviving consequence.

date_rule.basis: after EO 3259 (Apr. 16, 1920) and no later than EO 3265 (Apr. 29, 1920), which records the actual sale

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing
The held edge from EO 3265 (modification, 1920-04-29) is the evidence used, not a contradiction.
The sale's exact date is in the Custodian's reports (S17), not held.

procedure.description: EO 3233 (Tidewater Coal Exchange order reinstated) states its own end: midnight, April 30, 1920.

when.text_regex: remain in force and effect until midnight of the thirtieth

lead.basis: The order says it 'shall remain in force and effect until midnight of the thirtieth day of April, 1920, at which time, unless otherwise ordered, it shall cease to be operative'.

date_rule.basis: stated end, inclusive (runs through the end of April 30, 1920); exclusive reading: ends when that day begins

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing

'Unless otherwise ordered': no extension order between Feb. 25 and Apr. 30, 1920 is recorded in the WPA list or the held edges. EO 3233 carries held suspension and restoration edges from EO 3247 (1920-03-19), but EO 3247's words except it: the suspension reaches all later coal orders 'except the Executive order of February 25, 1920, relative to the Tidewater Coal Exchange' (S23, held). The edges misread EO 3247, fall before the stated end, and do not change the lead.

procedure.description: EO 6023 (air-space reservation over the District of Columbia) states its own period: 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. on March 4, 1933.

lead.basis: The order designates the air space over the District of Columbia a prohibited area 'from 9 a. m. to 5 p. m., on March 4, 1933' and nothing else. It is an inauguration-day reservation under the Air Commerce Act of 1926, not a defensive sea area.

gaps: Held text is OCR of the 1974 OFR compilation; no gap in the end itself.

procedure.description: EO 2929 (petroleum specifications through the Fuel Administrator) states its own term: the war and six months after its termination by the proclamation of a treaty of peace.

when.text_regex: six months after the termination thereof by the proclamation of a treaty of peace

lead.basis: The order says it remains in force 'during the continuance of the present war and for six months after the termination thereof by the proclamation of a treaty of peace, or until amended, modified, or rescinded'. The treaty with Germany was proclaimed Nov. 14, 1921 and the last treaty (Hungary) Dec. 20, 1921, so the term ran out no later than June 20, 1922.

date_rule.basis: from the printed date (31 July 1918; the census gives 1918-07-30) to six months after the last 1921 treaty proclamation; May 14, 1922 if 'a treaty of peace' means the German treaty; earlier if rescinded

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing
EO 3374 recites that the Fuel Administration's activities were suspended on or before Jan. 1, 1920, so the order's practical operation likely ended earlier; that recital is not a rescission.
The census dates EO 2929 1918-07-30; the held text is signed '31 July, 1918', which the interval uses.
The treaty proclamations (S5, S6) are read on the web and not held.

procedure.description: One act for one named person: designations of Edgar Rickard and Theodore F. Whitmarsh to act as Food Administrator in Hoover's absence, and appointments of George O. May and Charles Arthur Richards to the War Trade Board. They follow PD-CS-ONE-PERSON (COORDINATOR_RULINGS P4).

lead.basis: The order's operative content is one designation or appointment of one named person, so PD-CS-ONE-PERSON decides it. Disclosed candidate ends: the designations to act as Food Administrator end with the Food Administration, abolished by EO 3320 on Aug. 21, 1920 (held), or earlier when the absence ended; the War Trade Board seats end with the Board, which the National Archives records as abolished effective June 30, 1919 (not held).

gaps: Apply PD-CS-ONE-PERSON to these five orders; the candidate ends above are its inputs.

procedure.description: EO 2679-A (organizing the Food Administration) and EO 3087 (Wheat Director): EO 3320 terminated and abolished both by name.

lead.basis: COORDINATOR_RULINGS P7: EO 3320 (Aug. 21, 1920) abolishes by name the subject through which the member commands, and the member does nothing else that continues. It declares 'said United States Food Administration, and all remaining divisions and branches thereof, are hereby terminated and abolished' (the agency EO 2679-A organized, described in EO 3320 as 'a Government agency organized and conducted pursuant to Executive Orders and Proclamations of the President'), and 'the executive administration and office created by said Executive Order of May 14, 1919' (EO 3087, the Wheat Director) 'is hereby terminated and abolished'. EO 3087's other continuing words, the Grain Corporation's authority to buy and sell 1919 wheat, run 'with the approval of the United States Wheat Director'; EO 3320 confines the Corporation to liquidation, 'continuing to act as a governmental agency for this purpose only'. EO 3087's closing of the Corporation's books, its change of name and its capital increase were completed acts whose consequences belong to the Corporation's history.

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing
EO 3320 saved sugar licenses and sugar regulations already made; those are separate instruments, not EO 2679-A or 3087.
Acts done and ratified under these orders survive as consequences.
EO 2679-A carries held partial_modification edges from EO 2694-A (1917-09-02, 'so far as it is inconsistent herewith'); a partial modification before the end does not change the lead.

procedure.description: Orders that direct the Food Administrator, the Wheat Director, or the Grain Corporation as wheat-buying agency: EO 3320 abolished those offices and confined the Corporation to liquidation.

lead.basis: COORDINATOR_RULINGS P7: EO 3320 (Aug. 21, 1920) abolishes by name the subject through which the member commands, and the member does nothing else that continues. Each order commands only through those offices: EO 2736 (Hoover 'as Food Administrator' to requisition foods and feeds); EO 2884 (the Grain Corporation as wheat-buying agency 'subject to the control and direction of the United States Food Administrator'); EO 3100 (purchases by the Corporation 'under the direction of the United States Wheat Director'); EO 3143 (transfer from the Food Administrator to the Wheat Director). EO 3320 terminated and abolished the Food Administration and the Wheat Director's office and confined the Corporation to liquidation 'for this purpose only'. The commands ended no later than Aug. 21, 1920 (earlier if the office had already ceased to exercise them).

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing
EO 2884's increase of the Grain Corporation's capital stock is a completed act whose consequence lasted until the Corporation dissolved; only the continuing command is claimed ended.
EO 3143 invokes the Overman Act 'as well as ... any and all other acts of Congress'; its lead rests on the abolition of both offices it commands through (P7), not on the Overman Act's end.

procedure.description: Orders creating the Committee on Public Information and its divisions: ended with the Committee under EO 3154.

lead.basis: EO 3154 (held) provides that 'upon such relinquishment and transfer the Committee on Public Information shall cease and be at an end'; no held text shows the transfer made. The National Archives entry (RG 63, not held) reads 'Abolished: By EO 3154, August 21, 1919', which restates EO 3154's issue date and does not record the transfer. Orders creating the Committee or its divisions end when it does.

gaps: A record of the relinquishment and transfer itself (Council of National Defense records or the Committee's liquidation reports in NARA RG 63) would decide these as no, ended by EO 3154, dated by the transfer. The NARA finding aid alone supports the date only weakly.
EO 2594 carries a held cross_reference edge from EO 3154 (Wikisource note 'Obsoletes Executive Order 2594'); an editor's note is not the instrument's words.

procedure.description: EO 2913 (Labor Secretary to use Squares 229 and 230 for war housing): revoked by EO 2952.

lead.basis: EO 2952 (Sept. 6, 1918) revokes and rescinds 'the Executive Order issued July 15, 1918' authorizing the Secretary of Labor to use Squares 229 and 230; EO 2913 is that order (EO 2912 of the same day concerns Squares 685 and 634).

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing
The census dates EO 2952 only to '1918'; its printed date Sept. 6, 1918 is from the held scan.

procedure.description: EO 2837 (revoking Treasury and Federal Trade Commission licensing powers on enemy patents and trade-marks, with 'no such license shall be granted until further order'): rescinded by EO 3180.

lead.basis: Besides revoking two licensing powers, EO 2837 forbade such licenses 'until further order', a continuing command. EO 3180 (Nov. 25, 1919, a family member) rescinds 'as of the 14th day of July, 1919, the Executive Order of April 11, 1918' and confirms licenses issued from that day.

date_rule.basis: EO 3180 issued Nov. 25, 1919, rescinding as of July 14, 1919

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing

procedure.description: Orders whose only operative content is a delegation of Lever Act powers (fuel, distilled spirits, licensee profits, coal rules) and which rest on the Lever Act alone.

not.text_regex: any and all other|all other powers|other powers vested in me

lead.basis: COORDINATOR_RULINGS P8. The order rests on the Act of Aug. 10, 1917 alone and its only operative content is a delegation of powers that Act gave the President: EO 2690 the Fuel Administrator's office and powers (sec. 25 and the fuel provisions), EO 2694-A Treasury supervision of distilled spirits (secs. 2, 15, 16), EO 2765 the Food Administrator's licensee-profit rules (sec. 5), EO 3173 the Fuel Administrator's power to restore, change or make coal rules. Sec. 24 provides that 'the provisions of this Act shall cease to be in effect when the existing state of war between the United States and Germany shall have terminated', the fact and date to be 'ascertained and proclaimed by the President'; 41 Stat. 1359-1360 displaces that mode ('notwithstanding any provision ... providing any other mode of determining the date'), fixes March 3, 1921, and does not except the Lever Act. The ceasing words reach the very provisions delegated, so the delegate has nothing left to exercise; sec. 24 saves only acts done and rights accrued, which are consequences. This is not a repeal of the authority to make new orders (FLPMA sec. 704(a)), where existing orders keep effect of their own.

date_rule.basis: no later than the Lever Act's cessation under 41 Stat. 1359

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing

EO 3247 suspended EO 3173 (with all later presidential coal orders except EO 3233) from Apr. 1, 1920 'until otherwise ordered'; a suspension is not an end, so the claimed end stays no later than March 3, 1921.
EO 2694-A's clause modifying the Food Administration order 'so far as it is inconsistent herewith' is incidental to the delegation.
EO 2765 is here, not under EO 3320, because EO 3320 saved sugar licenses and sugar regulations.
No presidential proclamation under sec. 24 was searched for; 41 Stat. 1359-1360 makes one unnecessary.

procedure.description: Orders under the Lever Act or the emergency shipping fund that do more than delegate, or that also invoke other authority: EO 3247 (a presidential suspension of coal orders), EO 2825-A (Navy to take possession of equipment on Netherlands ships, adopting earlier takings and directing compensation), EO 3063 (redelegation plus a direction to transfer contracts and a ratified payment), EO 3235 and EO 3240 (coal powers of the Director General of Railroads, resting on the Lever Act 'and other powers vested in me by law' or 'all other powers me hereto enabling').

lead.basis: Each order rests on a statute whose powers ceased (Lever Act by March 3, 1921; emergency shipping fund by May 14, 1922), but either its operative content is not only a delegation (it suspends other orders, commands takings and compensation, or directs a transfer of contracts) or it also rests on other powers that the ceasing words do not reach (EO 3235, 3240). Under COORDINATOR_RULINGS P3 and P8 the cessation is a disclosed earlier candidate end, not an end.

gaps: Performance of EO 2825-A's takings and compensation and of EO 3063's contract transfer.
EO 3247: an instrument ending the suspension or the suspended orders (their own end does not by itself end the suspending order's command).

EO 3235 and 3240: what 'other powers' they rest on (for example the Director General of Railroads' powers under federal control of the railroads) and when those ended; both were suspended by EO 3247 from Apr. 1, 1920 'until otherwise ordered', and EO 3240 acts 'in the present emergency'. Candidate end: March 3, 1921 for their Lever Act part.

procedure.description: Orders whose only operative content is a delegation of the President's powers under the emergency shipping fund section of the Act of June 15, 1917, as amended by the Act of Apr. 22, 1918.

when.text_regex: emergency shipping fund|June 15, 1917|fifteenth, nineteen hundred and seventeen

lead.basis: COORDINATOR_RULINGS P8. EO 2664 delegates the section's powers to the Emergency Fleet Corporation and the Shipping Board; EO 2888 delegates to the Emergency Fleet Corporation 'all power and authority vested in me by' the Act of Apr. 22, 1918, 'An Act to Amend the emergency shipping fund provisions of the Urgent Deficiency Appropriation Act, approved June fifteenth, nineteen hundred and seventeen'. That Act amends the 1917 section 'by adding a new provision' and by adding words to its paragraph (b), and has no termination provision of its own, so its powers are part of the section. The section provides: 'All authority granted to the President herein, or by him delegated, shall cease six months after a final treaty of peace is proclaimed between this Government and the German Empire.' The treaty was proclaimed Nov. 14, 1921, so the delegated authority ceased no later than May 14, 1922 (Sept. 3, 1921 if 41 Stat. 1359 governs the clause).

date_rule.basis: six months after Nov. 14, 1921; Sept. 3, 1921 if 41 Stat. 1359 governs the clause

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing

Whether a later statute extended or ended the fund's authority has not been fully checked. EO 3549 (held) quotes sec. 17 of the Merchant Marine Act of June 5, 1920, which directed the Shipping Board to take over on Jan. 1, 1921 the piers and terminals the President acquired under the 1918 deficiency act; that moves property, and its effect on the delegated authority is unread. An earlier end would still fall inside the interval, an extension would not.
EO 2664 carries held edges from EO 3018 (1918-12-03, extension); EO 3018 supplements the delegation before the end, which does not change the lead.

The reading that powers inserted into the 1917 section by the Act of Apr. 22, 1918 fall within 'herein' is the ordinary one for amending text (it becomes part of the amended section); it is disclosed for EO 2888.

procedure.description: EO 3018 and EO 3064: delegations of powers under several Acts 'establishing, enlarging and maintaining the Emergency Shipping Fund', including sections of the Acts of July 1, 1918 and Nov. 4, 1918 that have not been read.

lead.basis: EO 3018 delegates 'all the power and authority so vested in me' by the June 15, 1917 section, the Oct. 6, 1917 section, the Act of Apr. 22, 1918 and the 'Emergency shipping fund' sections of the Acts of July 1, 1918 and Nov. 4, 1918; EO 3064 withdraws part of the power so delegated and delegates it to the Secretary of War. The 1917 section's cessation sentence reaches authority granted 'herein'. The Apr. 22, 1918 Act amends that section and the Oct. 6, 1917 section only raises its cost limits, but the two 1918 sections have not been read, so whether their powers fall within 'herein' is unverified. The cessation (no later than May 14, 1922) is a disclosed candidate end.

gaps: Read the 'Emergency shipping fund' sections of the Sundry Civil Appropriation Act of July 1, 1918 (40 Stat. 634) and the First Deficiency Appropriation Act, 1919 (Nov. 4, 1918; page unverified). If they only enlarge the 1917 section's authority, both orders take B14's lead.
EO 3018 also ratifies past acts, a completed act.
EO 3064's subject (river barges and towboats for the Mississippi) may also have been affected by later inland-waterways legislation, not checked.

procedure.description: Orders whose only operative content is a reassignment of functions under the Overman Act and which rest on that Act alone: transfer of the War Trade Board's work to the State Department (EO 3059, 3086-A) and transfer of Navy war vessels (EO 3091).

not.text_regex: any and all other|all other powers|Chief Executive

lead.basis: COORDINATOR_RULINGS P8. The order rests on the Act of May 20, 1918 alone and its only operative content is a redistribution of functions that Act authorized. The Act remained in force 'during the continuance of the present war and for six months after the termination of the war by the proclamation of the treaty of peace, or at such earlier time as the President may designate', and provides: 'Upon the termination of this Act all executive or administrative agencies ... shall exercise the same functions, duties, and powers as heretofore or as hereafter by law may be provided, any authorization of the President under this Act to the contrary notwithstanding.' The latest reading of the duration ends June 20, 1922 (six months after the Hungarian treaty proclamation); under 41 Stat. 1359 it ends Sept. 3, 1921.

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing
The Act let the President designate an earlier end; none is recorded.
Completed acts under these orders (records and vessels transferred) are consequences, not continuing commands.
Disclosed earlier end for EOs 3059 and 3086-A: the National Archives (RG 182, not held) records the War Trade Board as abolished effective June 30, 1919 under them.

EO 3091 carries a held amendment edge from EO 3222 (1920-02-03), which extends it to the Panama Canal 'Under authority of the Act of Congress, Chapter 78, Section 2, approved May 20, 1918' alone; under P2 that text merges into EO 3091 and the amendment falls inside the interval, so the lead stands.

procedure.description: Overman Act orders that also invoke other authority: EO 3019-A (dissolution of the War Industries Board), EO 3161 (Council of National Defense to pay the Board's obligations), EO 3248-A (Interior to pay Fuel Administration claims from named appropriations), EO 3249 (liquidation of the Bituminous Coal Commission).

lead.basis: Each order rests on the Overman Act 'as well as by virtue of any and all other Acts of Congress conferring authority upon me in the premises' (EO 3019-A, 3161, 3248-A) or 'by virtue of all other powers thereto me enabling' (EO 3249). The Overman Act's termination words reach only 'any authorization of the President under this Act', so its end (no later than June 20, 1922) is a disclosed candidate, not an end of the whole order. EO 3019-A's own cap, 'in no event longer than the proclamation of peace', governs only its continuation of officials; its Price Fixing Committee continuation, transferred functions and winding-up continuation have no stated end, and the treaty proclamations are not held.

gaps: For each order, evidence that the other authority it invokes was spent (the named appropriations exhausted or lapsed, the liquidation completed): Council of National Defense and Interior liquidation records.
EO 3019-A: the treaty proclamation texts (S5, S6) would date the cap on its first exception; its other continuations need completion records.

EO 3249 carries a held cross_reference edge from EO 3283 (1920-06-16), which suspends its provision no. 3 (transfer of the Bituminous Coal Commission's records to Interior on June 30, 1920) 'until the conclusion of the work of the United States Anthracite Coal Commission'; that end is not held.

procedure.description: EO 2868 (War Industries Board made a separate agency): its Board was dissolved by EO 3019-A with continuations whose ends are not held.

lead.basis: EO 2868 rests on the Council of National Defense provisions of the Act of Aug. 29, 1916, not on the Overman Act. EO 3019-A, which recites the Board's creation, ordered the Board and its subordinate bodies to 'terminate and dissolve on' Jan. 1, 1919, but continued officials 'in no event longer than the proclamation of peace', the Price Fixing Committee until fixed prices expired, and the Board itself 'for the sole and only purpose of winding up'. Because the dissolution was not complete on Jan. 1, 1919 and the continuations' ends are not held, the abolition is a disclosed candidate end (P7 requires the subject's abolition; here part of it continued).

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing
The date the winding-up was completed (EO 3161 shows the Council of National Defense paying the Board's obligations by Aug. 1919); the treaty proclamation texts for the 'proclamation of peace' cap.

procedure.description: EO 2652 (watch officers' citizenship requirement suspended 'for the duration of the war'): own term keyed to the war.

when.text_regex: for the duration of the war

lead.basis: The suspension lets qualifying aliens serve as watch officers 'for the duration of the war'. The war the order refers to (with Germany) was declared at an end by the joint resolution of July 2, 1921 and closed by the treaty proclaimed Nov. 14, 1921; on any reading the stated duration ran out no later than Dec. 20, 1921, the last 1921 treaty proclamation.

date_rule.basis: from the printed date (July 3, 1917; the census gives 1917-06-03) to the war's end on the latest reading; earlier if revoked

gaps: order text is held only as a transcription or page scan; the operative clause relied on should be checked against an official printing
41 Stat. 1359 governs Acts, joint resolutions and proclamations, not an executive order's own words, so March 3, 1921 is not used as the date.
The census dates EO 2652 1917-06-03; the held Wikisource text is signed 'The White House, July 3, 1917', which the interval uses.
The Knox-Porter Resolution and the treaty proclamations (S5, S6, S7) are read on the web and not held.

procedure.description: Alien Property Custodian sale, rejection-of-bids, resale and release determinations (including Frank L. Polk's orders under EO 3016): single authorizations exhausted only when the act was done.

lead.basis: The order authorizes (or directs) one disposition of named property under sec. 12 of the Trading with the Enemy Act and sets no deadline. It is spent when the sale, rejection, resale or release is made, and no held record shows that it was made (the one order a held text shows performed, EO 3259, is decided by B03E). The Trading with the Enemy Act is excepted from the 1921 resolution and is still law, and the later transfers of the Custodian's functions (EO 6694 of 1934; EO 9095 and EO 9142 of 1942; EO 9788 of 1946; the 1966 abolition of the Office of Alien Property) moved the functions without extinguishing authorizations, so no class event ends an unexercised authorization.

gaps: The Custodian's report for 1918 to Feb. 15, 1919 and the annual reports for 1919-1934 (S17) would show the sale or rejection for each trust; until one is held the order stays open.
Property returned under the Settlement of War Claims Act of 1928 (45 Stat. 254; not held) would make an unexercised authorization moot; that would need its own evidence.
Orders covering several lots or properties need one end per lot.
EO 2832 is a general rule (private sale of merchandise in lots worth no more than $10,000), not a single authorization; it ends only by revocation or supersession, which is not held.

EO 4224-A's only operative clause is 'The Alien Property Custodian is hereby authorized to execute and deliver a quit-claim deed conveying certain interests in real estate' in Cook County, Illinois; amending EO 4073-A appears only among its stated reasons. It is its own single authorization, open here like EO 3923 and EO 4045.

EO 3183 (reject all bids at the Sept. 17, 1919 auction of the same 4,505 First Reinsurance shares): EO 3259 recites that the shares were 'thrice offered at public auction and no satisfactory bid has been received', and EO 3265 records their private sale to another buyer by Apr. 29, 1920. That shows the subject was disposed of by then, but no held text records that the Richter & Company bid was rejected; open pending a coordinator decision whether disposal of the subject ends an unexercised rejection authorization.

EO 3227 (Feb. 13, 1920) authorizes the Custodian to confirm 'in the case of sales heretofore made by him' under the Polk orders of Feb. 26, 1919 (EO 3016C) and Apr. 5, 1919 (EO 3016K). The words are conditional and name no property, so they do not show any particular sale made; EO 3016C, 3016K and 3227 stay open.

EO 3923 carries a held revocation edge from PLO 369 (May 15, 1947, 12 FR 2038; BLM table, PLO text not held): 'revoking EO Nos. 2247, 2658, and 3923; withdrawing lands for Agriculture experimental station'. EO 2247 and 2658 are Alaska agricultural-experiment-station orders; the held EO 3923 is a Custodian sale of Stoehr & Sons shares with no land to revoke. This is a number collision, so the edge does not decide this member; the PLO's '3923' should be traced in the census.
EO 4001 carries a held amendment edge from EO 4045 (1924-07-03); EO 4045 changes the parent's terms, not its performance, and both stay open.

procedure.description: Other orders under the Trading with the Enemy Act: delegations of powers to the Custodian, the Treasury, the Attorney General and the War Trade Board, and general rules.

lead.basis: The Trading with the Enemy Act is excepted from the 1921 resolution and remains in force; the order's delegations were carried forward by later transfers rather than ended, and no held instrument revokes the order as a whole.

gaps: A revocation or supersession of each delegation (for example by EO 6694 of 1934, EO 9095 or EO 9142 of 1942, or later delegations under sec. 5(b)) must be found and read; EO 6694's text is not held.

EO 2729-A is a multi-part order. Its Censorship Board part was ended by EO 3132 (B03). Its War Trade Board part has a disclosed candidate end: the National Archives records the Board as abolished effective June 30, 1919 under EO 3059 and 3086-A (S11, not held). Its other parts remain open.

EO 2729-A's held revocation edges are partial by their own words: EO 2801 revokes its paragraph XXX and substitutes a new one; EO 2837 revokes the Secretary of the Treasury's licensing power under its section XI (and EO 3180 later rescinds EO 2837); EO 3016 vests in Frank L. Polk the President's sec. 12 powers. None revokes EO 2729-A as a whole, so none decides it.
EO 2744 carries a held amendment edge from EO 3016 (1918-12-03); a partial change does not decide it.

EO 3016 carries held 'amendment' edges from EO 3016F, 3016P, 3016Q, 3016S, 3016T and 3016X: these are Frank L. Polk's sale and rejection orders, which recite EO 3016 as the source of his authority; they exercise the delegation rather than amend it. EO 2729-A also carries an amendment edge from EO 4862 (1928-04-23, supplemental); EO 2770 and 2796 carry cross-reference edges only. None ends a member.

procedure.description: Eight-hour-law suspensions or waivers for named work, contracts or agencies.

lead.basis: Each order suspends or waives the eight-hour law for named construction, contracts or purchase orders (EO 2656, 2663, 2678, 2769), for an agency's contracts 'during the present national emergency' (EO 2864, 2928), or for Shipping Board repair contracts 'until further order' (EO 3015). Two authorities are used. Sec. 2 of the Act of June 19, 1912 (37 Stat. 137, 138) is a war-contingent power to waive the Act 'as to any specific contract' 'during time of war or a time when war is imminent'; EO 2663 rests on it alone and EO 2678 on it with 39 Stat. 1192. The proviso of 39 Stat. 1192 is a power 'in case of national emergency'. 41 Stat. 1359 governs the construction of Acts whose provisions are contingent on the 1917 war or the 'present or existing emergency, meaning thereby the war'; whether it reaches either power is unsettled, and its words do not reach a waiver already granted for a specific contract, which is an exercise of the power and not a delegation (P8 does not apply). March 3, 1921 is therefore a disclosed candidate end for the waivers resting on the 1912 power, and completion of the work, or the end of the 'present national emergency' the orders speak of, is not recorded.

gaps: Completion records for the Post Office equipment shops (Washington), the Treasury buildings at 500-508 Fourteenth Street NW, the Alaska Railroad car contracts and the D.C. fuel yards; a revoking order for EO 3015; an instrument fixing the end of the 'present national emergency' for EOs 2864 and 2928.
Whether 41 Stat. 1359 reaches sec. 2 of the 1912 Act or the 39 Stat. 1192 proviso, and if so whether a waiver granted before March 3, 1921 lapsed with it.

procedure.description: Single acts and transfers whose performance is not recorded: seizure or transfer of named vessels, piers and transports, appraisal boards, transfers of records, property and funds, disposal of materials, and the CPI transfer itself.

lead.basis: The order commands a single act (take over a vessel, transfer piers, ships, records or funds, appoint an appraisal board) or a continuing custody arrangement; it is spent only when performed, and no held record shows performance and its date.

gaps: Shipping Board and Navy annual reports (vessels, piers, transports), NARA administrative histories (records transfers), and the Housing Corporation's reports (EO 2912, 2952, 3296) would show performance. EO 2859-A has no held text.

procedure.description: Catch-all: agencies and government corporations that continued under later liquidation (Grain Corporation EO 2681 and 3320; U.S. Housing Corporation EO 2985-A, 3408), radio and cable control (2585, 2605-A, 2604), the consular-fee order 'during the continuance of the war and until further orders' (2826), and other continuing war orders (2616, 2645, 2687, 2874, 3017, 3053-A).

lead.basis: No ending basis that reaches the order is held: its authority is not shown to have ended with a statute that reached it, or it created a body whose dissolution date is not held, or its own term is ambiguous.

gaps: Grain Corporation and Housing Corporation dissolution records; the return of radio stations and the end of cable censorship; reading of EO 2826's 'and until further orders'.

EO 2687 is a mixed order: its delegation of the emergency shipping fund powers ended under M7 (no later than May 14, 1922), but its delegation of the 'Naval emergency fund' powers of the Act of Mar. 4, 1917 needs that section's own terms, which have not been read.

EO 3017 needs the Act of July 18, 1918's termination clause. Its held amendment edge from EO 3800 (1923-03-02) is spurious: EO 3800 enlarges the Mount McKinley National Park administrative site and amends a different order of Jan. 13, 1922.

EO 2645 carries a held supersession edge to EO 2687-A (Aug. 21, 1917) that rests only on a Wikisource editor's note ('Superseded by Executive Order 2687-A, August 21, 1917'); EO 2687-A's text is not held. Under P3 the supersession must be read in EO 2687-A's own words before it ends EO 2645; Aug. 21, 1917 is a disclosed candidate end. Title VII of the Espionage Act, on which EO 2645 rests, has not been read for a war-contingent end.
EO 2604 carries held amendment edges from EO 2967 and EO 3030 (P2 members merged into it).

undecidable.reason: Alien Property Custodian sale, rejection, resale and release orders: performance is in the Custodian's reports, not held.
Trading with the Enemy Act delegations and general rules: the Act is excepted from 41 Stat. 1359 and in force; supersession not yet read.
Eight-hour suspensions and waivers: completion of the work not recorded; the 1921 resolution's reach to the 1912 and 1917 powers unsettled.
Single acts and transfers whose performance is not recorded.
Committee on Public Information orders: the end is conditional on a transfer that no held record dates.
One act for one named person: follows PD-CS-ONE-PERSON.
Orders on ceased statutes whose content is more than a delegation, or which also invoke other authority: cessation is only a candidate end.
Emergency shipping fund delegations under 1918 sections not yet read.
War Industries Board order whose subject was dissolved with continuations of unheld end.
Bodies in liquidation, communications control, ambiguous own terms, statutes not yet read, an editor's note of supersession.
Misclassified members (families named), a member whose held text is another order's, and a number without record.
